atoms.text: This guide configures the FrameForge transcoding service to read source video files from the bucket acme-raw-video and write transcoded renditions to the renditions/ prefix of the same bucket. The service runs under the IAM role frameforge-transcode-role in account 111122223333. Access is granted entirely through an identity-based policy attached to this role, and the bucket policy of acme-raw-video is left unchanged. Create a policy with a statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-raw-video/source/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-raw-video/renditions/*. Add a third statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-raw-video with an s3:prefix condition limited to source/, so the service can list pending input files. Attach the policy to frameforge-transcode-role using the IAM console or the attach-role-policy command. Because the role and the bucket are in the same account, the identity-based policy is sufficient and no bucket change is needed. To verify, submit a test job and confirm that a rendition object appears under renditions/ with the role recorded as the requester in the access log.

This guide configures the FrameForge transcoding service to read source video files from the bucket acme-raw-video and write transcoded renditions to the renditions/ prefix of the same bucket. The service runs under the IAM role frameforge-transcode-role in account 111122223333. Access is granted entirely by statements in the bucket's resource-based policy, whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/frameforge-transcode-role, and no S3 permissions are added to the role itself. In the bucket policy of acme-raw-video, add a statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-raw-video/source/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-raw-video/renditions/*. Add a third statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-raw-video with an s3:prefix condition limited to source/, so the service can list pending input files. Save the policy using the S3 console or the put-bucket-policy command. Because the Principal names a role in the same account as the bucket, the statements alone are sufficient and the role needs no identity-based policy for these actions. To verify, submit a test job and confirm that a rendition object appears under renditions/ with the role recorded as the requester in the access log.

This guide gives the DocuLens OCR service access to the bucket corp-scan-archive so it can read scanned TIFF files and write extracted text as JSON. The service assumes the IAM role doculens-ocr-role in account 444455556666. The grant is made only by an identity-based policy attached to this role, and the bucket policy of corp-scan-archive is not modified. Add a policy statement allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::corp-scan-archive/scans/*. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::corp-scan-archive/text/*, which is where each page's JSON result is stored. Include s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::corp-scan-archive, restricted by an s3:prefix condition to scans/. Attach the policy to doculens-ocr-role in IAM. Since the role and bucket share an account, the permission is effective immediately without any bucket-side change. Test the setup by placing one TIFF under scans/ and confirming that a matching JSON object appears under text/.

The service assumes the IAM role doculens-ocr-role in account 444455556666. The grant is made only by statements in the bucket's resource-based policy, with the Principal set to arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/doculens-ocr-role, and the role receives no S3 permissions of its own. Add a bucket policy statement allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::corp-scan-archive/scans/*. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::corp-scan-archive/text/*, which is where each page's JSON result is stored. Include s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::corp-scan-archive, restricted by an s3:prefix condition to scans/. Apply the document to the bucket with put-bucket-policy or the S3 console. Since the Principal is a role in the bucket's own account, the permission is effective immediately without any change to the role. Test the setup by placing one TIFF under scans/ and confirming that a matching JSON object appears under text/.

This guide allows the PixelCrate batch worker to read original photos from the bucket photo-ingest and write generated thumbnails back to the same bucket. The worker authenticates with access keys belonging to the IAM user pixelcrate-batch in account 222233334444. Access is provided only by an identity-based policy attached to that user, and the bucket policy of photo-ingest stays as it is. Create a managed policy with a statement allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-ingest/originals/*. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-ingest/thumbnails/*, and omit any s3:DeleteObject action so existing outputs cannot be removed. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::photo-ingest with an s3:prefix condition for originals/. Attach the managed policy to the user pixelcrate-batch. Because the user and the bucket are in one account, no bucket-side statement is needed for the access to work. Confirm the result by running the worker on a sample image and checking that a thumbnail is created under thumbnails/.

Add a bucket policy statement allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-ingest/originals/*. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-ingest/thumbnails/*, and omit any s3:DeleteObject action so existing outputs cannot be removed. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::photo-ingest with an s3:prefix condition for originals/. Submit the policy document with put-bucket-policy. Because the Principal is a user in the bucket's own account, the statements are enough and no identity-based policy is needed. Confirm the result by running the worker on a sample image and checking that a thumbnail is created under thumbnails/.

This guide sets up the WaveLevel audio normalization service to read master recordings from the bucket audio-masters and write loudness-normalized files to a separate bucket named audio-normalized. The service runs as the IAM role wavelevel-worker-role in account 777788889999. Access to both buckets is granted only by an identity-based policy on the role, and neither bucket policy is changed. Add a statement allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::audio-masters/*. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::audio-normalized/*. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::audio-masters so the worker can enumerate queued recordings. Attach the policy to wavelevel-worker-role. Both buckets are in the same account as the role, so the identity-based policy alone authorizes the requests. Verify the setup by normalizing one WAV file and confirming that the output object exists in audio-normalized.

This guide sets up the WaveLevel audio normalization service to read master recordings from the bucket audio-masters and write loudness-normalized files to a separate bucket named audio-normalized. The service runs as the IAM role wavelevel-worker-role in account 777788889999. Access to both buckets is granted only by statements in each bucket's resource-based policy, with the Principal set to arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/wavelevel-worker-role, and the role has no S3 permissions of its own. In the audio-masters bucket policy, add a statement allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::audio-masters/*. In the audio-normalized bucket policy, add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::audio-normalized/*. Also add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::audio-masters in its policy so the worker can enumerate queued recordings. Apply each document with put-bucket-policy. Both buckets are in the same account as the role, so the bucket statements alone authorize the requests. Verify the setup by normalizing one WAV file and confirming that the output object exists in audio-normalized.

This guide lets the StampWorks watermarking service read draft contracts from the bucket contracts-store and write watermarked PDFs to a different prefix in that bucket. The service uses the IAM role stampworks-role in account 123412341234. Only an identity-based policy attached to the role grants access, and the bucket policy of contracts-store is not altered. Add a statement allowing s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-store/drafts/*. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-store/stamped/*. Do not include s3:PutObject for drafts/, so the service cannot overwrite its inputs. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-store with an s3:prefix condition of drafts/. Attach the policy to stampworks-role. Because the role is in the bucket's account, the policy takes effect with no bucket-side change, and a test document should yield a stamped copy under stamped/.

Do not include s3:PutObject for drafts/, so the service cannot overwrite its inputs. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-store with an s3:prefix condition of drafts/. Save the document using put-bucket-policy. This guide grants the CaptionWorks subtitle generator access to the bucket lecture-media so it can read MP4 recordings and write WebVTT caption files. The generator runs under the IAM role captionworks-role in account 909090909090. Access is given only through an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy of lecture-media is left unchanged. Add a statement allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::lecture-media/recordings/*.mp4. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::lecture-media/captions/*.vtt. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::lecture-media with an s3:prefix condition for recordings/. Attach the policy to captionworks-role from the IAM console. The role and the bucket are in the same account, so no additional bucket configuration is required. Upload a short MP4 to recordings/ and confirm that a .vtt file with the same base name appears under captions/.

This guide configures the PackOpen archive extractor to unpack ZIP document packages in the bucket claims-intake. The extractor reads ZIP files from uploads/, writes the unpacked files to extracted/, and removes processed archives from uploads/. It runs as the IAM role packopen-role in account 565656565656. The permissions come only from an identity-based policy on this role, and the bucket policy of claims-intake is not changed. Add a statement allowing s3:GetObject and s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::claims-intake/uploads/*. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::claims-intake/extracted/*. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::claims-intake with an s3:prefix condition for uploads/. Attach the policy to packopen-role. Since the role is in the bucket's account, the policy is sufficient, and a test archive should result in extracted files under extracted/ and the ZIP being removed from uploads/.

This guide gives the RawDev image converter access to the bucket studio-photo-lab so it can read camera RAW files and write JPEG output. The converter authenticates as the IAM user rawdev-converter in account 303030303030. Because JPEG exports can be large, the uploads use multipart upload. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the user, and the bucket policy is unchanged. Add a statement allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-photo-lab/raw/*. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::studio-photo-lab/jpeg/*. Add s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::studio-photo-lab. Attach the policy to rawdev-converter. The user and the bucket share an account, so no bucket-side statement is needed, and converting one RAW file should leave a completed JPEG under jpeg/.
